extracted.intended_audience: authors, maintainers, and distributors of software, LaTeX packages, and documentation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory conditions for distributing, modifying, and maintaining software (GPL), LaTeX-related works (LPPL), and documentation/manuals (GFDL). Covers applicability, required notices, source distribution, copyleft obligations, maintainer rules, and warranty disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL applicability (what counts as the Program)
rubrics_metrics.description: This License applies to any program or other work which contains a notice placed by the copyright holder saying it may be distributed under the terms of this General Public License. The 'Program' refers to any such program or work, and a 'work based on the Program' means either the Program or any derivative work under copyright law: that is to say, a work containing the Program or a portion of it, either verbatim or with modifications and/or translated into another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation is included without limitation in 'modification'. Each licensee is addressed as 'you'.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL scope: running vs distribution/modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities other than copying, distribution and modification are not covered by this License; they are outside its scope. The act of running the Program is not restricted, and the output from the Program is covered only if its contents constitute a work based on the Program (independent of having been made by running the Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether program output is a 'work based on the Program' depends on what the Program does; running the program imposes no license obligations.

rubrics_metrics.description: You may copy and distribute verbatim copies of the Program’s source code as you receive it, in any medium, provided that you conspicuously and appropriately publish on each copy an appropriate copyright notice and disclaimer of warranty; keep intact all the notices that refer to this License and to the absence of any warranty; and give any other recipients of the Program a copy of this License along with the Program.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements apply to the modified work as a whole; see exceptions for independent sections and interactive-program exceptions noted in the license text.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL: exception for independent sections and aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: If identifiable sections of that work are not derived from the Program, and can be reasonably considered independent and separate works in themselves, then this License, and its terms, do not apply to those sections when you distribute them as separate works. Mere aggregation of another work not based on the Program with the Program on a medium does not bring the other work under the scope of this License.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL: distribution in object code/executable form (source obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may copy and distribute the Program (or a work based on it) in object code or executable form ... provided that you also do one of the following: (a) accompany it with the complete corresponding machine-readable source code distributed under the terms of Sections 1 and 2; or (b) accompany it with a written offer, valid for at least three years, to give any third party, for a charge no more than your cost of physically performing source distribution, a complete machine-readable copy of the corresponding source code; or (c) accompany it with the information you received as to the offer to distribute corresponding source code (allowed only for noncommercial distribution and only if you received the program in object code with such an offer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing any of these options meets the GPL's source-distribution requirement for distributing binaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL: definition of 'source code' and 'complete source'
rubrics_metrics.description: The source code for a work means the preferred form of the work for making modifications to it. For an executable work, complete source code means all the source code for all modules it contains, plus any associated interface definition files, plus the scripts used to control compilation and installation of the executable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special exception: the distributed source need not include anything normally distributed with major components (compiler, kernel) of the operating system unless that component itself accompanies the executable.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL: offering equivalent access counts as source distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If distribution of executable or object code is made by offering access to copy from a designated place, then offering equivalent access to copy the source code from the same place counts as distribution of the source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties are not compelled to copy the source along with the object code, but the availability satisfies the obligation.

rubrics_metrics.description: You may not copy, modify, sublicense, or distribute the Program except as expressly provided under this License. Any attempt otherwise is void, and will automatically terminate your rights under this License.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPL: acceptance by conduct

Therefore, by modifying or distributing the Program (or any work based on the Program), you indicate your acceptance of this License to do so, and all its terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.description: The LaTeX Project Public License (lppl) is the primary license under which the LaTeX kernel and the base LaTeX packages are distributed. You may use this license for any work of which you hold the copyright and which you wish to distribute; it is suitable for TEX-related works but can be used more generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL definitions (Work, Derived Work, Modification, Distribution, Compiled Work, Current Maintainer, Base Interpreter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions used in the license: 'Work' any work being distributed under this License; 'Derived Work' any work derived from the Work; 'Modification' any procedure that produces a Derived Work; 'Distribution' making copies available; 'Compiled Work' a version processed into a directly usable form; 'Current Maintainer' person(s) nominated as such; 'Base Interpreter' program normally needed to run or interpret the Work (default LATEX-Format unless specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: scope — running not restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities other than distribution and/or modification of the Work are not covered by this license; they are outside its scope. In particular, the act of running the Work is not restricted and no requirements are made concerning any offers of support for the Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running and use impose no license obligations under LPPL.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: distribution of complete unmodified Work only
rubrics_metrics.description: You may distribute a complete, unmodified copy of the Work as you received it. Distribution of only part of the Work is considered modification of the Work, and no right to distribute such a Derived Work may be assumed under the terms of this clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributing parts of a Work without the whole is treated as creating a Derived Work and triggers modification conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: compiled works from unmodified Work
rubrics_metrics.description: You may distribute a Compiled Work that has been generated from a complete, unmodified copy of the Work as long as that Compiled Work is distributed in such a way that the recipients may install the Compiled Work on their system exactly as it would have been installed if they generated a Compiled Work directly from the Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure installation behavior and content match what recipients would get by compiling themselves from the unmodified Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: Current Maintainer privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are the Current Maintainer of the Work, you may, without restriction, modify the Work, thus creating a Derived Work. You may also distribute the Derived Work without restriction, including Compiled Works generated from the Derived Work. rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: non-maintainer modification and distribution conditions (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not the Current Maintainer of the Work, you may modify your copy of the Work, creating a Derived Work, and compile this Derived Work. If you distribute a Derived Work, certain conditions must be met for every component of the Work unless that component clearly states exemption by the Current Maintainer.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL (6a): replacement component identification (interactive use)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a component of this Derived Work can be a direct replacement for a component of the Work when that component is used with the Base Interpreter, then, wherever this component of the Work identifies itself to the user when used interactively with that Base Interpreter, the replacement component of this Derived Work clearly and unambiguously identifies itself as a modified version of this component to the user when used interactively with that Base Interpreter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive identification prevents disguised replacements and protects users from unnoticed modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL (6b): change notices or change-log requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every component of the Derived Work contains prominent notices detailing the nature of the changes to that component, or a prominent reference to another file that is distributed as part of the Derived Work and that contains a complete and accurate log of the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominent change notices or a comprehensive change-log file must be included to make modifications visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL (6c): no implied support by original authors
rubrics_metrics.description: No information in the Derived Work implies that any persons, including the authors of the original version of the Work, provide any support to recipients of the Derived Work unless those persons have stated explicitly that they do provide such support for the Derived Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim original authors provide maintenance/support unless explicitly agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL (6d): distribution requirement — provide unmodified Work or info to obtain it
rubrics_metrics.description: You distribute at least one of the following with the Derived Work: (i) a complete, unmodified copy of the Work; or (ii) information that is sufficient to obtain a complete, unmodified copy of the Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: distributing compiled works from Derived Works
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not the Current Maintainer of the Work, you may distribute a Compiled Work generated from a Derived Work, as long as the Derived Work is distributed to all recipients of the Compiled Work, and the conditions of Clause 6 are met with regard to the Derived Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: exception for making a component identical to an updated version
rubrics_metrics.description: The conditions above do not apply to the modification of any component so that it becomes identical to an updated version of that component of the Work as it is distributed by the Current Maintainer under Clause 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronizing a component to the current maintainer's updated version does not trigger the 'Derived Work' restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: permitting different license for Derived Work that honors Clause 6
rubrics_metrics.description: A Derived Work may be distributed under a different license provided that license itself honors the conditions listed in Clause 6 above, in regard to the Work. If distributed under a different license, that Derived Work must provide sufficient documentation as part of itself to allow each recipient to honor the restrictions in Clause 6 concerning changes from the Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: maintenance status and how to become Current Maintainer
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and rules for 'author-maintained', 'maintained', and 'unmaintained' status. A Work is 'maintained' if a Current Maintainer is indicated and willing to receive error reports. It becomes 'unmaintained' if no Current Maintainer is reachable for six months and no signs of active maintenance exist. Steps to become Current Maintainer include reasonable attempts to contact existing maintainer, announcing intent to the pertinent community, and rules for immediate effect if the current maintainer agrees or the copyright holder consents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you become Current Maintainer, promptly provide a prominent unambiguous statement in the Work and announce to the pertinent community.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: recommendation — avoid untracked personal modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is wise never to modify a component of the Work, even for your own personal use, without also meeting the above conditions for distributing the modified component, because such modifications may be accidentally distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep your copy identical with the public one; many works provide ways to control behavior without altering licensed components.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: how to apply the license to your work (required notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use this license, place in each of the components of your work both an explicit copyright notice including your name and the year the work was authored and/or last substantially modified, and a statement that the distribution and/or modification of that component is constrained by the conditions in this license.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPPL: defining what constitutes the Work (manifest recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lppl requires that distributions of the Work contain all the files of the Work. It is therefore important that you provide a way for the licensee to determine which files constitute the Work, e.g., by explicitly listing all the files of the Work near the copyright notice of each file or by using a line such as '% This work consists of all files listed in manifest.txt.'

rubrics_metrics.name: GFDL purpose and copyleft principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this License is to make a manual, textbook, or other functional and useful document 'free' in the sense of freedom: to assure everyone the effective freedom to copy and redistribute it, with or without modifying it, either commercially or noncommercially. This License is a kind of 'copyleft', which means that derivative works of the document must themselves be free in the same sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: GFDL: applicability and definitions (Document, Modified Version, Secondary and Invariant Sections, Cover Texts, Transparent copy, Title Page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'Document' any manual or other work with a GFDL notice; 'Modified Version' any work containing the Document either verbatim or with modifications/translation; 'Secondary Section' named sections dealing exclusively with publisher/author relationship to subject; 'Invariant Sections' are Secondary Sections designated in the license notice; 'Cover Texts' short front/back cover passages; 'Transparent copy' a machine-readable format suitable for editing; 'Title Page' meaning for printed and non-printed formats; 'Entitled XYZ' definition for preserving section titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: GFDL: Opaque copies in quantity must include Transparent copy or location
rubrics_metrics.description: If you publish or distribute Opaque copies of the Document numbering more than 100, you must either include a machine-readable Transparent copy along with each Opaque copy, or state in or with each Opaque copy a computer-network location from which the public can download a complete Transparent copy of the Document using public-standard protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: GFDL: conditions for distributing a Modified Version
